episodes.167619: A slow moving low pressure system, along with plenty of moisture, allowed for showers and thunderstorms to gradually move through the Ohio Valley during the day on May 6th. Heavy rainfall occurred with these storms and additional storm and shower activity developed over the same areas. A swath of 3 to 4 inches of rain fell in a narrow corridor from Huntington northeastward to Elkins, with a few isolated pockets of 4 to 5 reported. This led to considerable flash flooding. A few stronger storms also developed, one of which led to an area of tree damage in Randolph County.||Multiple water rescues took place throughout the Metro Valley, including a man who was swept away while working on his tractor in Cabell County. Additionally, several vehicles were submerged in flood waters and over one hundred homes were impacted by high water with the hardest hit area being the Enslow Park community of Huntington. Flooding occurred across many roadways throughout West Virginia, leaving multiple roads impassable for a time until the water receded.||Even after the rain had concluded, several rivers in the state rose out of their banks for the next several days. This resulted in flooding along areas adjacent to the rivers.
episodes.167756: An unseasonal cold upper-level trough and associated front moved through Northwest California. The system brought lower snow levels and post-frontal hail showers. Small hail covered roadways caused a couple of accidents.
episodes.167842: A line of severe thunderstorms developed over south central South Dakota, producing strong wind gusts over parts of Tripp County.
episodes.168183: Storms formed in the Missouri River Valley in the afternoon producing quarter to half dollar sized hail. These storms merged into a line which would eventually produce three weak tornadoes. One of these tornadoes destroyed a shed near Columbia. The system moved east of the James River Valley in the evening with limited severe weather thereafter. Additionally, heavy rain caused flooding in Edmunds county which had already seen minor water issues due to persistent early May rainfall. Some strong to high non-thunderstorm gusts also occurred with this system, including 66 mph in Agar and 57 mph in both the Polo and Summit areas.
episodes.168565: Isolated thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon hours of May 7th over the northern Nebraska Panhandle. Storms developed in advance of an approaching cold front which lifted across western and central Nebraska during the nighttime hours. As storms tracked east of the panhandle, they organized into a line of strong to severe thunderstorms which stretched from north central Nebraska into southwestern Nebraska. Hail up to golf ball size and wind gusts to around 70 MPH were reported.
episodes.168665: Showers and thunderstorms developed during the early morning hours in an area of weak, confluent southwesterly flow.  Isolated gale-force wind gusts occurred offshore Islamorada.
episodes.168666: An isolated, yet mature, waterspout was observed just north of the Seven Mile Bridge as nocturnally-enhanced showers and thunderstorms were beginning to dissipate.
episodes.169199: During the first week of the month, two storm systems moved out of the southern Plains. Scattered showers and thunderstorms brought around an inch of rain on average, while a few locations received up to 2.5 inches. Rises on the Mississippi River were sufficient for some minor flooding in a few areas.
episodes.169267: Overnight thunderstorms across Nebraska moved into Iowa in the early morning hours of May 8th. The nocturnal storms we fueled in part by the low level jet, and continued to be sustained by steady moisture transport across the area. As storms moved across the Des Moines metro, a lightning strike is believed to have started a fire which caused significant damage to several condos. By afternoon some strengthening occurred and while thunderstorms remained below severe limits, penny sized hail was reported with one storm.
episodes.169296: On May 7th, a cold front passed through far southwestern Nebraska, which allowed for isolated severe thunderstorms to develop in the area. These thunderstorms yielded wind gusts up to 70 mph within the area.
episodes.170276: Scattered thunderstorms moving through the area south of a cold front produced gusty winds over the nearshore Atlantic waters.
episodes.170296: A line of thunderstorms crossing a warm front caused several instances of flooding across MD on May 6th into May 7th. Residual river flooding continued through May 9th due to excessive runoff.
episodes.170301: A line of thunderstorms crossing a warm front caused several instances of flooding across MD on May 6th into May 7th. Residual main stem river flooding continued through May 9th.

events.narrative: A thunderstorm wind gust of 43 mph (37 knots) was recorded at the WxFlow station XPEG in Port Everglades.
Hail lasted for 5 minutes. Time estimated by radar.
Overland flooding resulted from intense thunderstorm rainfall, as reported on social media. 2.27 inches of rain was measured nearby.

In the town of Little, Middle Island Creek rose out of its 14 foot bankfull level and remained out of its banks until the early morning hours of May 8th. The creek rose to 14.47 feet, which resulted in minor flooding along Stewarts Run Road and within the field located opposite of the gage.

The West Fork River in Clarksburg rose above its 14 foot flood stage on the evening of May 7th and remained in flood until the early morning hours of the 8th. The river crested at 14.31 feet, which resulted in minor flooding of low lying areas along the river as well as water spilling onto Liberty Avenue.
A tornado touched down in an open dirt field and lingered there for less than a minute.
A security camera captured a brief tornado touchdown in an open field.
A brief funnel cloud was reported by an emergency manager.
A weak tornado demolished a shed, but no other damage was noted to the surrounding buildings.
Power lost at this location along with nickel sized hail. Time estimated by radar.

The stream gage on the Potomac River in Shepherdstown exceeded flood stage during the specified timeframe, reaching a crest of 20.00 ft on May 8th at 3:30 PM EST.  At this level there are significant impacts on either side of the Potomac. Large portion of the C&O Canal towpath are flooded. Additionally, water comes out of its banks at the mouth of the Opequon. Impacts felt near the river in the city of Shepherdstown as well.

The stream gage on Conococheague Creek near Fairview indicated flooding during the specified timeframe, reaching a crest of 10.19 ft on May 8th at 5:30 AM EST. At this level both Wishard Road and Kemp Mill Road are flooded.

Public reports multiple 3 to 5 inch tree limbs down at this location blocking a road. Time estimated by radar.

The KMCK ASOS located 2 miles of McCook, NE recorded northerly wind gusts up to 70 mph on the southern periphery of a supercell thunderstorm.  Five minute sustained winds of 40 to 50 mph were recorded during this time by the ASOS as well.

The stream gage on the Potomac River at Edwards Ferry indicated that flooding occurred for a period of around 43 hours, reaching a peak crest of 18.45 ft at 6:45 PM EST on May 9th. At this level the parking lot at Edwards Ferry is completely covered by water. The parking lot at Seneca is partially flooded. Additionally, floodwaters have entered the store at Whites Ferry.

events.county: Hawk Channel From Ocean Reef To Craig Key Out To The Reef
events.narrative: A southwest wind gust of 36 knots was observed at the WeatherFlow station at Alligator Reef Light.

The stream gage on the Potomac River at Point of Rocks indicated that flooding occurred during the specified timeframe, reaching a peak crest of 18.29 ft at 7:30 PM EST on May 8th. At this level, there are several instances of flooding right along the river between Point of Rocks and Brunswick, with water approaching the structures at Brunswick Family Campground. Many islands within the Potomac river are flooded at this point as well. Many boat ramps and nearby parking lots are flooded at this stage as well.

At 201 Grand Avenue, three condos suffered major damage and a fourth had minor damage from a fire believed to have been started by lightning according to firefighters. Time estimated using lightning data.

events.county: Bayside And Gulfside From Craig Key To West End Of Seven Mile Bridge
events.narrative: A mature waterspout was reported just north of the Seven Mile Bridge.  The narrow condensation funnel cloud extended almost the entire way from cloud base to the waters surface and a spray ring was visible.  The waterspout was tilted at about a 45-degree angle midway up to the cloud base while moving eastward.  The location was estimated based on radar and satellite imagery.
Non-injury accident due to small hail on roadway near the intersection of Highway 101 and Central Avenue.
Photo of a nickel next to a slightly smaller hail stone.

The stream gage on the Potomac River indicated that flooding occurred during the specified timeframe, reaching a peak crest of 10.16 ft at 10:45 PM on May 8th. At this stage, impacts are largely felt right along the river banks and at some of the islands in the Potomac itself. Several sections of trail right near the river will be closed, and Sycamore Island starts to see impacts as waters reach the canoe shed.
